boundaries.label: The mechanism — input, loop, output, and the rule that keeps it learning
Who does the work — the same shift at founder and team scale

cards.title: The hub and the mechanism
items: AI-Native Company is the frame: AI is the operating system the company runs on, token usage replaces headcount as the binding constraint, and the intelligence layer takes over middle management's routing role.

The mechanism is a triangle. Organizational Legibility is the input: if an action was not recorded, it did not happen to the AI, and recordings must be synthesized down because no context window holds an org's history.

Self-Improving AI Loop is the unit of work: a process wrapped in a closed feedback loop that fixes its own failures. Fix the Principle, Not the Example keeps a loop learning instead of accumulating patches.

Company Brain is the output: business context and skills are the durable asset, and accumulated context compounds into a moat. The one idea to remember: recorded context lasts; everything else, including the software, is disposable.

cards.title: Who does the work, what gets rebuilt
items: AI-Native Role Archetypes: hire for judgment because models supply throughput; role boundaries blur; every agent workflow still has a named human owner.
Founder as Orchestrator and Everyone Ships are the same shift at founder and team scale: the person who understands the problem ships the first version.

Prototype, Dogfood, Productionize is the path an internal tool takes to become product; Build for Rebuilding says the software on top is discarded each model generation, which only makes sense if the context in the brain is what persists.
AI-Native Startup Lifecycle remaps the four startup stages on the same premise: each stage no longer needs a bigger team and a fresh round.

cards.title: Where the tensions are
items: One intelligence layer or a mesh: AI-Native Company says the intelligence layer replaces middle management's routing; Company Brain carries a contested, low-confidence claim that large organizations get a mesh of sources of truth agents reconcile. A source on an org past a few hundred people would settle it.

Disposable software, durable context: Build for Rebuilding and Company Brain only agree if code and context are kept strictly apart. No page states that separation as its own claim; this KB's Three-Layer Architecture is one instance of it.

Roles blur, owners stay: AI-Native Role Archetypes and Everyone Ships say boundaries dissolve and anyone ships, yet require a named human owner per workflow and say the division of labor survives past the first version. Which roles survive is not stated.

Thin sourcing: AI-Native Startup Lifecycle rests on one vendor ebook, Founder as Orchestrator and Everyone Ships on vendor-curated testimonials; their supported status is weaker than it reads. Prototype, Dogfood, Productionize has no claim callout at all.

cards.title: Sourcing
items: Two YC talks (Hu, Blomfield) are VC prescription; the Anthropic playbooks and the Startups guide are vendor prescription and vendor-curated testimonials; the Claude Code team's account is the one first-party practitioner source.
The AI Daily Brief episode is the first non-YC, non-Anthropic source and mostly corroborates pages that already existed.
Strongest claims: the two high-confidence legibility claims. Most in doubt: one layer or a mesh. Every other claim in the cluster is medium confidence.
